newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares soar 3.72 pct in strong rebound.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares soar 3.72 pct in strong rebound.

text.p: Istanbul shares surged amid selective buys on Tuesday in a strong recovery that followed Monday's 2.44 percent fall due to S&P's donwgrading of Turkey's long-term foreign currency rating last Friday.
The IMKB-100 closed 3,239.00 points, or 3.72 percent higher at a day's high of 90,395.96.
Trade volume jumped to 19.17 trillion lira, including a 1.84 trillion lira block deal on the wholesale market, from Monday's 10.58 trillion.
Brokers said lively selective activity continued in the second session following a 3.31 percent morning jump.

"The market will try to keep the index at around 90,000 levels although there is caution ahead of the constitutional court's decision on the Telekom sell-off," said Huseyin Istanbullu from Meksa securities.

The court began debating a challenge to a law concerning Turk Telekom's privatisation last Tuesday. It is not known when it will rule. The planned Turk Telekom sell-off constitutes a large part of the government's envisaged non-tax revenues for 1997.

The index had sank 5.5 percent at Monday's opening in strong selling after the S&P cut Turkey's long-term foreign currency rating to "single B" from "single B-plus". It recouped part of its losses later on Monday as support emerged at 84,000.
The market had also shed 5.37 percent last week amid negative expectations ahead of the S&P downgrade and stiff resistance at the index's 95,000 mark.

Of the 231 shares traded, gainers outdid losers sharply by 183 to 14 and 34 closed stable. The 85-share industrial index surged 3.93 percent to 96,289.64 and the 15-share financial index jumped 3.24 percent to 85,905.79.

Leading actives were utilities Cukurova Elektrik, up 5,000 lira at 93,000, Aktas Elektrik, up 4,000 lira at 82,000 and largely state owned flat steel giant Eregli, up 750 lira at 12,000. They made up 19.7 percent of the total turnover.
